unmapped_findings: Measured chemistry from Table I (wt.%): Si 1.07, C 0.90, Mn 30.42, P 0.001, S 0.006, Mo 0.53, Al 8.83, Cu 0.006 (balance Fe). [b0013]

The solution-treated 0.001% P Charpy V-notch specimen failed by ductile micro-void coalescence, in contrast to the 0.07% P specimen's low-energy cleavage-like fracture producing a dendritic pattern (Fig. 8). [b0043, figure_008]
Solution-treated notch toughness is stated in the text as 200 J for the 0.001% P sample, while Table III lists 199 J for the same condition (147 ± 17 ft-lbs). [b0043, b0048]
AlN is the dominant inclusion type in the 0.001% P calcium-treated, argon-stirred alloy; higher AlN density correlates with lower CVN energy (Fig. 10). [b0056, figure_010]

Total inclusion density was 62–78 inclusions/mm² across the three low-phosphorus Si steels; the 1.07% Si steel had the lowest micro-defect/porosity density among 0.59/1.07/1.56% Si steels (Fig. 15). [b0079, b0081, figure_015]

Silicon additions (0.59–1.56% Si) have no significant effect on solution-treated mechanical properties; this sample's solution-treated strengths reach 737 MPa with 64% elongation. [b0004, b0035, b0085]
The lightweight Fe-Mn-Al-C steels are ~15% less dense than quenched and tempered SAE 4130 Cr-Mo steel. [b0004, b0085]
